thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/stream (prod-us-west). p95 = 820ms (SLO 300ms), p99 = 3.9s (SLO 1s). Streaming stalls observed; reconnects spiking. Affected model: rwdx-14b-stream (hosted). 
lee_oncall: Acknowledged. I'm oncall for prod-us-west. Pulling traces and dashboards now. Any customer pages?
maya_infra: I'm seeing coincident GPU node degradation on cluster gpu-pool-3: node gpus-3a-07 showing rising ECC correctable errors and thermal fan RPM drops. Kernel logs show repeated PCIe resets.
sam_runtime: Repro on tracing: long tail correlates with a subset of streaming sessions hitting the same backend shard (shard-17). KV cache misses spike concurrently.
rachel_sre: Customer impact: ~1.8% of calls in the window 13:02:14-13:07:30 returned >2s; 0.6% hit >5s. We should consider paging customers flagged as SLA-sensitive.
eva_hw: From remote telemetry, GPU temps on gpus-3a-07 transiently hit 92C before fan command fails; card reports correctable ECC counts jumping by ~400 over 5m. Might be flaky hardware.
lee_oncall: Runbook step 1: move traffic off shard-17 and enable fallback model variant. Can someone post exact commands?
sam_runtime: Copying minimal mitigation: 
```
# reroute requests away from shard-17 
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.reddo/api/v1/routing/shift" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL" -d '{"from_shards":[17],"to_strategy":"hot-standby"}'
```
Also increasing stream_worker count for shard replicas to reduce queueing.
maya_infra: Running node quarantine on gpus-3a-07 now: `kubectl cordon gpus-3a-07 && kubectl drain gpus-3a-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` . Starting replacement from spare pool.
lee_oncall: Thanks Maya. After drain, please confirm new capacity and if autoscaler picked up spares.
maya_infra: Autoscaler spun up 2 replacement nodes (gpus-3a-12/13). Routing shows 85% of shard-17 rerouted within 35s.
rachel_sre: Notifying affected enterprise customers via status page draft: "We observed increased tail latency affecting a small subset of streaming requests in US-WEST between 13:02–13:10 UTC. Mitigation in progress, will update." Approve? :eyes:
eva_hw: Opening ticket with HW vendor and attaching ECC logs: TICKET-9876. Initial hypothesis: intermittent VRAM ECC flare coupled with fan controller failing to keep RPM under load.
ops-bot: Incident timeline entry created: INC-2026-03-15-296000.link(https://incidents.redwood/in/INC-2026-03-15-296000).
lee_oncall: Quick follow-up checks: p99 for other regions?
sam_runtime: p99 for eu-west and ap-south normal (sub-1s). This looks localized to us-west gpu-pool-3.
rachel_sre: SLA exposure: estimate 0.04% of monthly requests breached SLA due to this event window. Flagging for postmortem.
maya_infra: Node replacement healthy but I still see sporadic packet drops between NIC and host on the decommissioned node; suspect firmware flake.
eva_hw: For short-term, recommend marking the affected card as quarantined and blacklisting its PCI slot in BMC until vendor RMA. Applying soft-fan profile for same-generation nodes to avoid hitting hysteresis.
lee_oncall: Live mitigation checklist complete: traffic rerouted, node drained, replacement nodes up, customers notified draft ready. Keep monitoring for recurrence.
sam_runtime: I'll keep a short-term metric alert for p99>1.5s for 5m on any shard to auto-trigger additional routing. Adding a temporary circuit-breaker to streaming clients to reduce queue buildup.
rachel_sre: I'll coordinate post-incident report and include customer communications and estimated cost impact.
eva_hw: ETA from vendor unclear; they requested full log bundle (attached link). I'll start an RMA if counts keep growing.
lee_oncall: Good work. If no new regressions in 15m, we'll de-escalate and transition to long-term fix planning. Marking this thread for postmortem when closed. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: SYSTEM NOTE: Page acknowledged by lee_oncall at 13:03:02 UTC. Incident severity set to sev2.
ops-bot: Reminder: please fill the incident template here: https://wiki.redwood/ops/incidents/new with timeline and mitigation steps.
lee_oncall: Closing loop: 13:18 UTC p99 back down to 700ms after full drain + reroute, still above target but trending down. I'll update if anything else pops.
